proposed_claim: Public policy-document availability was low in the Manganello national screening snapshot.
manuscript_use: 13 of 100 policies detected; wording limited to source snapshot

proposed_claim: Non-compensatory mandatory questions are operationally plausible in higher-education procurement.
manuscript_use: Supports veto-gate design, not threshold or weight calibration
boundary: HECVAT is a questionnaire, not observed procurement outcomes.

proposed_claim: Higher-education AI procurement often lacks ongoing re-review and gives limited attention to bias.
Structured GenAI testing should identify risks, test them, and analyse results in context.
Published public-sector AI inventories may be stale or contain many tested rather than active systems.
manuscript_use: Supports source-versioning and lifecycle evidence maintenance

proposed_claim: The public consensus matrix can be audited structurally and qualitatively but cannot provide a single reproducible numerical benchmark.
evidence_location: Official 67-page supplement; 378-row consensus table; Figure 2; Table 3
manuscript_use: Report 378-row completeness, score distribution, construct crosswalk, and exact lineage discrepancies
boundary: No FAIGRI score calibration or external validation; raw coder matrices unavailable.

proposed_claim: An independent educational-AI governance checklist converges with the FAIGRI-X-EG construct set while retaining additional technical and societal dimensions.
manuscript_use: Supports coverage of privacy, fairness, transparency, human oversight, institutional accountability, monitoring, and redress
boundary: Qualitative crosswalk only; no item-score conversion, weighting, or validation claim.

proposed_claim: In a purposive education-relevant ATRS subset, public documentary coverage can remain partial even for production-phase systems, so deployment phase is not a substitute for documentary sufficiency.
evidence_location: Eight official ATRS pages; 40-row documentary-coverage trace; phase summary
manuscript_use: Report 31 Direct, 9 Partial, 0 None cells and that none of four Production records documented all five areas directly
boundary: Descriptive single-analyst purposive subset only; no population, causal, validation, or implementation-effectiveness inference.

proposed_claim: The Government of Canada AI Register provides broad structured inventory disclosure but its released schema does not explicitly require fairness/accessibility or human-review/appeal fields.
manuscript_use: Report field completeness, 33-record education/training subset, and explicit schema gaps
boundary: Schema absence is not control absence; no compliance or effectiveness inference.

proposed_claim: A fuller public-sector assessment instrument requires risk, impact, bias, privacy, audit, recourse and mitigation evidence beyond a minimum inventory register.
evidence_location: Risk areas and mitigation areas on official AIA page
manuscript_use: Contrast MVP register fields with 65-risk/41-mitigation assessment structure
boundary: No assumption that every register system falls within AIA scope.

proposed_claim: Higher-education procurement attention is strongest for data security/compliance and weaker for algorithmic bias and ongoing post-procurement review.
manuscript_use: Report 86% security, 86% compliance, 30% bias and 36% ongoing-review aggregates with qualifiers
boundary: Rounded non-institution-linked responses; no representative or causal inference.
